title: One Decade of Rustls: Evolution, Benchmarks, and Future Roadmap
gist: Ten years after its May 2016 start, the Rust TLS library Rustls now outperforms OpenSSL and BoringSSL on nearly every published benchmark (2,357 full handshakes/sec/core vs OpenSSL's 1,713 and BoringSSL's 1,302), funded into sustainability by ISRG's Prossimo, AWS and CNCF-backed Cure53 audits, with a 0.24 release promising split-mode throughput doubling before a stable 1.0.

themes.theme: Funding converts a grassroots project into infrastructure

insights.claim: Rustls shifted from a grassroots effort driven by independent contributors including Brian Smith and Dirkjan Ochtman into a sustainably funded open-source project with dedicated maintainers, which enabled full-time work on robustness, architecture refactoring and compliance features.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Targeted funding is the causal variable turning security-critical OSS into dependable infrastructure — relevant to open-source supply-chain risk assessments.

insights.claim: External contributions and targeted funding through ISRG's Prossimo initiative, Amazon Web Services and CNCF-backed third-party audits by Cure53 accelerated development and introduced modern features including post-quantum cryptography, FIPS certification and Encrypted ClientHello.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: FIPS certification plus post-quantum support removes the last procurement blockers for Rustls in regulated environments.
insights.locator: Initiated in May 2016, the project progressed rapidly

insights.claim: The 0.23 release line sustained dozens of non-breaking iterations, which developer communities on Reddit and Hacker News cite as evidence of disciplined API management.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: API stability, not just performance, is what drives dependency adoption in security libraries — a leading indicator of ecosystem lock-in.
insights.locator: The project’s recent trajectory has been anchored

themes.theme: Benchmark leadership over OpenSSL and BoringSSL

insights.claim: On x86_64, Rustls 0.23.37 delivers 2,357 full TLS handshakes per second per core, outperforming OpenSSL 3.6.1 at 1,713 (1.38x slower) and BoringSSL at 1,302 (1.82x slower).
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Memory safety no longer costs performance in the TLS layer — removes the main technical objection to displacing OpenSSL at the edge.

insights.claim: For resumed handshakes Rustls leads at 7,249 per second per core versus BoringSSL's 5,687 (1.28x slower) and OpenSSL's 3,780 (1.92x slower), a nearly 2x gap over OpenSSL.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Resumption throughput dominates real CDN and API-gateway workloads, so this is the number that translates to server-count savings.

insights.claim: In throughput Rustls achieves 7,333 megabytes received per second per core versus OpenSSL at 6,238 and BoringSSL at 6,218, while for data sent BoringSSL marginally leads at 7,565 MB/s/core against Rustls at 7,421.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: The only remaining BoringSSL advantage is a 2% send-side edge — effectively parity, so switching costs dominate the decision.

insights.claim: The upcoming 0.24 release shifts to external buffering via a new TlsInputBuffer trait so input arrives through that mechanism and output appends to user-provided vectors, enabling in-place decryption and eliminating redundant memory copies.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Zero-copy I/O design is where the next tier of TLS performance gains comes from, not cryptographic primitives.

insights.claim: Release 0.24 introduces a split mode, first requested by the community in 2019, that decouples post-handshake traffic into separate SendTraffic and ReceiveTraffic objects operating independently on different threads via a low-contention internal back-channel, allowing full-duplex applications to effectively double their throughput.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A claimed 2x for full-duplex workloads is a material cost lever for proxies and streaming infrastructure.
insights.locator: To maximise performance under full-duplex workloads

insights.claim: Version 0.24 addresses asynchronous programming via session types that model handshake states sequentially, allowing handshakes to run in blocking, async or completion-based styles.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Runtime-agnostic async design widens the set of embedding platforms, including io_uring-style completion runtimes.

insights.claim: Release 0.24 decouples cryptography providers into separate crates such as rustls-aws-lc-rs and rustls-ring, removing build-feature unification panics and allowing global providers to be configured externally.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Pluggable crypto backends let organisations swap in FIPS-validated providers without forking — a compliance-adoption unlock.
insights.locator: Furthermore, the 0.24 release decouples cryptography providers

insights.claim: Following stabilisation of 0.24, maintainers plan to transition toward a stable 1.0 API designed for long-term maintenance.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A 1.0 commitment is the trigger event for conservative enterprise adoption of Rustls over OpenSSL.
insights.locator: Following the stabilisation of the 0.24 release
